input.quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement commits a three-year term (SOW Attachment 1 § 2.0 mirrors it) and Section 5.0 provides termination only "for cause" under § 5.1, so IBM as customer has no convenience exit — a deviation in any term longer than 12 months. § 6.1 (p0722) lets IBM cancel Purchase Orders at any time, but that is order-level only and preserves cost reimbursements, so it is not an Agreement-level convenience right; the six-month (Base) and twelve-month (SOW) notices are renewal-blocking and belong under RENEWAL. The Vendor-side preferred element is already met: MSL may terminate only for cause during the committed term (the ancillary confidentiality agreement's mutual notice right at p1497 terminates only that exchange agreement). The single inserted § 5.4 now states the right in express checklist language — "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience", 30 days' prior written notice, and a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees — with "Customer" defined for that Section only as IBM, since "Customer" is otherwise undefined here and the SOW uses "IBM Customer Order" for IBM's own customers. No partial-termination wording, fee cap, or other extras were added.

ops.text: Termination for Convenience by Customer. For purposes of this Section 5.4, "Customer" means IBM. Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to Customer, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by Customer for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need an exit right: the three-year term currently lets IBM leave only for cause or by giving six months' notice against renewal. We have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, consistent with our preferred position; MSL's exit remains for cause or non-renewal only.
proposal.summary: Add Customer (IBM) termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
